:::{#exm-mixture-gaussian}
#### A two-component normal mixture

Let ${\p_1}$ be the $\ndist{0, 1}$ density and ${\p_2}$ the $\ndist{6, 1}$ density,
with mixing weights $w_1 = 0.3$ and $w_2 = 0.7$,
and let $X$ have density ${\p_{\text{mix}}} = 0.3\,{\p_1} + 0.7\,{\p_2}$.

- **Mean.**
  By @thm-mixture-mean and the [normal means](random-variables.qmd#thm-normal-moments),

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{X} &= 0.3 \cd 0 + 0.7 \cd 6 \\
  &= 4.2.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- **Density.**
  ${\p_{\text{mix}}}$ has peaks near the two component means,
  ${\p_{\text{mix}}}(0) \approx 0.120$ and ${\p_{\text{mix}}}(6) \approx 0.279$,
  with a trough between them, ${\p_{\text{mix}}}(3) \approx 0.004$.
  The density at the mean, ${\p_{\text{mix}}}(4.2) \approx 0.055$,
  is less than half its value at either peak.
- **Responsibilities.**
  By @thm-mixture-posterior,
  at $x = 3$, halfway between the component means,
  ${\p_1}(3) = {\p_2}(3)$ by the symmetry of the normal density, so:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \P(C = 2 \mid X = 3)
  &= \frac{0.7\,{\p_2}(3)}{0.3\,{\p_1}(3) + 0.7\,{\p_2}(3)} \\
  &= \frac{0.7}{0.3 + 0.7} \\
  &= 0.7,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  the prior weight: an observation equally far from both components
  carries no information about which component it came from.
  At $x = 4.2$, the same formula gives $\P(C = 2 \mid X = 4.2) \approx 0.9997$.

:::
